### KeySql

```ts
type KeySql = Readonly<{
  exec: (statement, ...bindings) => KeySqlCursor;
}>;
```

Synchronous SQL execution the key store runs its statements against. This shape
fits Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite (`state.storage.sql`) as is. A
`node:sqlite` adapter for hosts outside a Durable Object lives at
`@fungi.computer/ear-tag/keys/node`, kept out of this module so a Worker
consumer of this type never needs Node's own types to typecheck.

### KeyRefusal

```ts
type KeyRefusal = Readonly<{
  code: KeyRefusalCode;
  retryAfterSeconds?: number;
}>;
```

One closed refusal, carried as data rather than a thrown error type.

`invalid` means the caller's own input failed the operation's schema; it is the
caller's bug. `denied` means well-formed input was refused on its merits (no
authority, revoked, suspended). `unavailable` means the store could not read
back its own state (a corrupt row, a corrupt rate limit, or any other failure
that is not one of the other closed reasons); that is the store's own fault,
never the caller's, and every such failure is also logged before this outcome is
returned.

### IssuerAuthority

```ts
type IssuerAuthority<Capability> =
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "unrestricted";
    }>
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "bounded";
      grants: readonly Grant<Capability>[];
    }>;
```

What an issuing actor may grant. `"unrestricted"` may grant any capability in
the host's vocabulary; `"bounded"` may grant only a subset of its own live
grants, checked with the vocabulary's `isSubset`.

### createKeyStore()

```ts
function createKeyStore<Capability>(options): KeyStore<Capability>;
```

Create one tenant-scoped key store: bearer-key issuance, verification and
lifecycle over one host's capability vocabulary. One store instance is one
tenant; namespacing between tenants is the host's own table or storage boundary,
not a column inside this store.
